**Refined prompt:** Design the delta that gives `Comment` an `author`, as a solutioning architect on this RealWorld API — a spec a developer implements with zero design decisions left open, citing the current code, covering data model, capture, serialization, and the authorization consumer it unblocks, delivered as decisions-with-rejected-alternatives, invariants, impact, numbered open questions, and rollout/rollback, no implementation code. · **Assumptions:** this is the `comment.author` prerequisite called out in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`, so I scope it to the relation + its rendering and sequence the `DELETE` 403 enforcement as a separate dependent phase rather than folding it in; and I hold the comment response shape (`{article}` on create) unchanged, leaving that to the spec-conformance item.

---

# Design — `comment.author`

## What exists today

`Comment` (`src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15`) has `id`, `body`, and a `@ManyToOne` to `ArticleEntity`. No user column, no relation. `ArticleService.addComment()` sets `comment.body` and nothing else (`article.service.ts:104-106`). `findComments()` returns `article.comments` raw off the eager relation (`article.service.ts:165-168`, eager declared at `article.entity.ts:40`). `CommentsRO.comments` is typed by a file-local `interface Comment { body: string }` (`article.interface.ts:3-5`).

---

## Decision table

| # | Decision | Rejected alternative | Why it lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D1** | Add `author: UserEntity` to `Comment` as a `@ManyToOne` → FK column `authorId`, mirroring `ArticleEntity.author` (`article.entity.ts:37-38`) | Denormalised `authorUsername: string` column | `username` has no unique index (`schema.md:16`) and `PUT /user` can change it (`user.service.ts:74-81`), so a copied username rots silently — and the spec's `author.bio/image/following` still need the user row anyway |
| | | Plain `authorId: number` column with no relation, like `FollowsEntity` (`follows.entity.ts`) | Every read would need a hand-written second query. `ArticleEntity.author` is the nearest sibling and it is a real relation; "mirror the nearest sibling, never invent a pattern" |
| **D2** | Unidirectional — **no** `comments: Comment[]` inverse on `UserEntity` | Add `@OneToMany comments` to `UserEntity` | No endpoint needs "all comments by a user". Worse: `UserService.update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)` after deleting only `password` and `favorites` (`user.service.ts:74-81`) — a new relation array on the entity is one more property a request body can clobber (LESSONS #112) |
| **D3** | Column is **nullable at the DB level**; presence is enforced in the service, not the schema | `nullable: false` | `synchronize: true` (`ormconfig.json.example:9`) runs DDL at boot and there are no migration files (`schema.md:8-9`). Adding NOT NULL to a `comment` table that already has rows fails the boot or backfills an invalid FK. There is no migration step in which a backfill could run first |
| **D4** | `ArticleController.createComment` takes `@User('id') userId: number`; service signature becomes `addComment(userId, slug, commentData)`; service loads the user by id and assigns it to `comment.author` | `@User() user` — pass the whole object | `req.user` is `UserService.buildUserRO()`'s plain object (`user.service.ts:116-127`) carrying a freshly minted `token`; it is not a `UserEntity` and assigning it to a relation persists garbage. Every other handler takes `@User('id')` (`article.controller.ts:34,52,94,102`) |
| | | Read `authorId` from the request body | Client could forge any author. The route is already guarded (`article.module.ts:28`) so the middleware-supplied identity is available and authoritative |
| | userId is the **first** parameter | `addComment(slug, userId, ...)` | `favorite(id, slug)` / `unFavorite(id, slug)` (`article.service.ts:131,147`) put the caller first; match them |
| **D5** | `comment.author` is **not** eager; loaded explicitly where a comment payload is built | `{eager: true}` on `comment.author` | `ArticleEntity.comments` is already eager (`article.entity.ts:40`), so eager-author adds a `user` join per comment to *every* article load — `findAll`, `findOne`, `favorite`, `unFavorite`, `update` — and embeds user rows (password hash included) into the raw `ArticleEntity` returned inside `ArticleRO`, which nothing maps. Non-eager confines the exposure to paths that deliberately load it |
| **D6** | `findComments()` is rewritten to query `commentRepository` filtered by the resolved article id with `relations: ['author']`, instead of reading `article.comments` | Keep `article.comments` and load each author afterwards | N+1, and the eager-comments path yields `author === undefined` (LESSONS: "a relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`"), which the mapper would then have to treat as anonymous — hiding a load bug behind the same branch as a legitimately author-less legacy row (D3) |
| **D7** | Comment payloads are built by an explicit private mapper in `ArticleService` returning plain objects — never a raw entity | `@Exclude()` + `ClassSerializerInterceptor` | No interceptor exists anywhere (`main.ts:1-21`, `app.module.ts:10-22`); registering one changes serialization for every endpoint at once, including article responses that currently do return the password. The house pattern is hand-built RO objects (`profile.service.ts:35-39`, `user.service.ts:116-127`) |
| | | `delete user.password` on the loaded entity, as `ProfileService.findOne()` does (`profile.service.ts:25-26`) | Mutates a managed entity that may be saved later in the same request (`addComment` saves at `article.service.ts:110`) — the LESSONS #88 shape. It also leaves `email` in |
| | | Constrain the join with `select`/QueryBuilder | `comments` is eager, so those loads never pass through a QueryBuilder; a select list cannot reach them without rewriting every article read |
| **D8** | Author is rendered as `ProfileData` — `{username, bio, image, following}` — imported from `../profile/profile.interface` | Reuse `UserData` (what `ArticleData.author` is typed as today, `article.interface.ts:17`) | `UserData` carries `email` and `token` (`user.interface.ts:1-7`). The spec's comment author is a profile |
| | | Redeclare the shape locally inside `article.interface.ts` | Two definitions of the profile contract drift the moment `following` semantics change. Article→profile is already an established import direction (`article.module.ts:7`) |
| **D9** | Rename the file-local `interface Comment` (`article.interface.ts:3-5`) to an exported `CommentData` and widen it to `{ id, body, author }`; `CommentsRO.comments: CommentData[]` | Keep the name `Comment` | It shadows the entity class, which `article.service.ts:5` imports under exactly that name — any future co-import collides. `CommentData` matches `ArticleData`/`UserData`/`ProfileData` in the same codebase |
| **D10** | `following` is computed in `ArticleService` from the already-injected `followsRepository` (`article.service.ts:22-23`), with **one** `find({followerId: userId})` per request and a set membership test per comment | Call `ProfileService.findProfile()` per author | `ArticleModule` does not import `ProfileModule` (`article.module.ts:12-13`); pulling it in for a three-field mapping is a module dependency for nothing, and `findProfile` issues a query per author — N+1 across a comment list |
| **D11** | `GET /articles/:slug/comments` gains `@User('id') userId: number`; when it is `undefined` (anonymous caller) `following` is emitted as **`false`**, not omitted | Omit the key when anonymous, as `findProfile` does (`profile.service.ts:43-45`) | The route is public (absent from `article.module.ts:23-31`). RealWorld frontends read `author.following` as a boolean; `undefined` happens to be falsy, but LESSONS #99 says diff against the spec's object shape, and the spec's shape has the field. Optional-auth-on-a-public-route is already the house pattern (`profile.controller.ts:19`) |
| **D12** | A legacy comment with `author === null` (D3) serializes as `author: null` | Substitute the article's author | Inventing attribution writes a falsehood into the API. See OQ-1 — this is a data decision, not a design one |
| | | Omit the comment from the list | Silently changes `GET .../comments` result counts on existing data |
| **D13** | `CreateCommentDto` is unchanged; `addComment` keeps copying fields by name | Accept an author field / `Object.assign(comment, commentData)` | LESSONS #112. The current by-name copy is the reason a forged `author` in the body is already inert — preserve that property rather than re-earning it |
| **D14** | `POST /articles/:slug/comments` keeps returning `{article}` (`article.service.ts:111`) in this delta | Change it to the spec's `{comment}` now | That is a response-contract change belonging to the spec-conformance item (`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`); bundling it makes the author change non-revertible on its own. See OQ-5 |
| **D15** | The `DELETE` 403 check ships as a **second commit**, after the relation and after OQ-1 is answered | One commit: relation + enforcement | Legacy rows have `author === null`. The moment the comparison lands, every pre-existing comment becomes undeletable by everyone. The relation must exist and the backfill must be decided before enforcement is safe |
| **D16** | No change to `article.module.ts` | Register new repositories | `ArticleEntity`, `Comment`, `UserEntity` and `FollowsEntity` are all already in `forFeature` (`article.module.ts:13`) and all four repositories are already injected (`article.service.ts:15-24`). Nothing new is needed |

---

## Invariants preserved

1. **The RO envelope.** `CommentsRO` stays `{comments: [...]}`; `addComment`/`deleteComment` keep returning `ArticleRO`. No handler starts returning a bare entity (LESSONS #57).
2. **No password or email in any response that does not already contain one.** D5 + D7 together guarantee the new relation is only ever materialised behind the mapper. The pre-existing leak in `findAll()` is neither widened nor fixed — see OQ-6.
3. **The guarded-route set is unchanged.** `article.module.ts:23-31` is not edited. Author capture happens only on a route that is already authenticated; author rendering happens on a route that stays public.
4. **`ArticleEntity.comments` stays `{eager: true}`.** `addComment` (`:107`) and `deleteComment` (`:118-122`) both read `article.comments`; removing eager breaks them.
5. **Comment ids are stable.** Additive column only; no table rebuild. `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` keeps resolving existing ids.
6. **Layer order.** Controller passes `@User('id')`; all resolution, follows lookup and mapping stay in `ArticleService`; the controller gains no repository.
7. **Request bodies stay nested and field-copied.** `@Body('comment')` unchanged; no `Object.assign` introduced.

---

## Impact analysis

**Schema.** One nullable `authorId` int column + FK index on `comment`, created by `synchronize: true` at boot. No data migration required for the DDL itself.

**Endpoint-by-endpoint:**

| Endpoint | Change |
|---|---|
| `POST /articles/:slug/comments` | Now persists `authorId`. **Response bytes unchanged** — the eager `comments` on the returned `ArticleEntity` load without their author (D5), so the `{article}` payload gains no key |
| `GET /articles/:slug/comments` | Each comment gains `author`. Objects are now mapped rather than raw entities — today they serialize as `{id, body}`, after as `{id, body, author}`. Strictly additive |
| `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`, favourite/unfavourite/update | Unchanged. Confirmed by D5: without eager author, no article read emits a new join or a new key |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | Unchanged in phase 1. Still reads `article.comments` (eager, author absent), still performs no ownership check |

**Files touched:** `comment.entity.ts`, `article.interface.ts`, `article.service.ts` (`addComment`, `findComments`, new private mapper), `article.controller.ts` (`createComment`, `findComments`). Not `article.module.ts` (D16).

**New failure surface:** adding `@User('id')` to the public `findComments` route (D11) means a tampered or expired token on that route now hits `jwt.verify` inside the decorator (`user.decorator.ts:15`), which throws uncaught → 500 instead of 401 (LESSONS #79). This is not a new class of bug — `GET /profiles/:username` already has it (`profile.controller.ts:19`) — but the change extends it to one more route. See OQ-7.

**Query cost, `GET /articles/:slug/comments`:** one article lookup (unchanged) + one comment query with a `user` join + one `follows` query when authenticated. Constant, not per-comment.

---

## Numbered open questions

Each blocks the phase noted; none is resolved here.

1. **Backfill policy for existing `comment` rows** — attribute to the article's author, delete them, or leave `author: null` and accept a broken subset? *Blocks: phase 2 (D15).* *Owner: repo maintainer / whoever owns the deployed database.* Needs a production row count for `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comment` before it can be answered.
2. **Who may delete a comment** — the comment's author only, or the comment's author OR the article's author? The RealWorld spec is not explicit and both implementations exist upstream. *Blocks: phase 2.* *Owner: repo maintainer, against the spec.*
3. **Legacy null-author comments under the 403 check** — deletable by no one, or by the article's author as a fallback? Depends on OQ-1's answer but is a separate call. *Blocks: phase 2.* *Owner: same as OQ-2.*
4. **`comment.createdAt` / `updatedAt`** — the entity has neither and the spec requires both. Same change or the spec-conformance pass? They carry the identical `synchronize: true` + existing-rows problem as D3. *Blocks: nothing; changes phase 1's scope if folded in.* *Owner: repo maintainer — it belongs to `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`.*
5. **`POST /articles/:slug/comments` returns `{article}`, the spec says `{comment}`** — fold into this change or leave to the conformance pass (D14)? *Owner: repo maintainer.*
6. **Pre-existing: `GET /articles` returns the article author's password hash and email**, via `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')` (`article.service.ts:30`) with no mapper. Fix now under the same mapper pattern, or track as its own security item? *Owner: repo maintainer.* Deliberately untouched here.
7. **Align `ProfileService.findProfile()` to always emit `following: false`** for anonymous callers (it currently omits the key, `profile.service.ts:43-45`), so comment authors and profile responses agree — and wrap `jwt.verify` in the decorator per LESSONS #79 while touching it? *Owner: repo maintainer.*
8. **Does the deployed instance actually run `synchronize: true`?** Only `ormconfig.json.example` is in the repo; the real `ormconfig.json` is not. If production uses migrations, D3 can be revisited and a NOT NULL column with a backfill becomes available. *Blocks: D3.* *Owner: whoever runs the deployment.*

---

## Rollout

**Phase 1 — relation + rendering** (this design, single commit):
1. `Comment` gains the nullable `@ManyToOne author`.
2. `article.interface.ts`: `Comment` → exported `CommentData` with `author: ProfileData`; `CommentsRO` retyped.
3. `ArticleService`: private comment mapper; `addComment(userId, slug, dto)` resolves and assigns the author; `findComments(userId, slug)` queries `commentRepository` with `relations: ['author']` and batches the follows lookup.
4. `ArticleController`: `@User('id')` added to `createComment` and `findComments`.
5. Boot once — `synchronize` adds the column. Verify against a database that has pre-existing comment rows, not a fresh one.

**Verification gates before phase 2:** a comment created by user A reports `author.username === A`; the same read anonymously reports `following: false`; authenticated as a follower of A reports `following: true`; `GET /articles` and `GET /articles/:slug` responses are byte-identical to before the change; no response anywhere contains `password`.

**Phase 2 — the 403** (separate commit, gated on OQ-1/2/3): ownership comparison in `deleteComment`, plus the matching `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug` checks from `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`. Out of scope for this spec beyond its sequencing.

## Rollback

**Revert the service, controller and interface changes only — do not revert `comment.entity.ts`.** `synchronize: true` drops columns that no longer appear in entity metadata, so reverting the entity destroys every captured `authorId` at the next boot. Left in place the column is inert: nothing reads it, nothing writes it, and no response shape depends on it.

That makes phase 1 reversible without data loss, and re-rolling-forward is a code-only deploy. Once phase 2 ships, rollback is the same move — revert the comparison, leave the column — and the behavioural regression is back to "any authenticated user can delete any comment", i.e. today's behaviour, not a new failure.
